city_params.n_celdas_hint: Spatial resolution: more cells = smoother profiles but slower simulation. Does not change the model physics: population is set by land use (ΣH), not by the grid.
city_params.n_parcelas_hint: Each parcel ≈ {{dx}} m (Δx = length/n). More parcels, more resolution and a slower simulation; population (ΣH) does not change with n.
city_params.pendiente_hint: Corridor slope: it slows the bike toward the CBD (uphill) and favors it on the way back.
city_params.land_use_note: Stratum composition and population are defined in Land Use and feed this simulation (households per stratum → households per cell).
city_params.defined_in_land_use: The city (length, cells and slope) and its population (households per stratum) are defined in Land Use and feed this simulation.
city_params.largo_hint: Population fixed ({{pob}} hh): changing the length recomputes density (now {{rho}} pop/km).

economy_params.bencina_hint: Market price per litre, taxes included. Drivers pay for the litres they burn, and burn more per km when moving slowly: congestion also costs them in fuel.
economy_params.peaje_hint: Charge per km driven. Like fuel, it grows with distance; unlike fuel, it is city revenue and adds to social welfare. Parking is a flat cordon charge; the toll comes closer to the Pigouvian charge, because the congestion cost a trip imposes grows with the links it crosses.
economy_params.teletrabajo_hint: Scales each stratum’s telework rate, which is set in Calibration and defaults to 0: without a base rate, the factor has no effect. Those agents do not travel and leave peak demand: it is the only lever here that removes trips rather than reassigning them between modes.

car.num_pistas_hint: Only helps if cars are congested (high v/c). With low car demand, adding lanes barely changes anything.
car.cap_manual_hint: Fixed capacity: raising speed no longer increases it (S-04).
car.cap_greenshields: Greenshields capacity: {{cap}} veh/h per lane (∝ free-flow speed — raising v_max also raises capacity).
car.bpr_practica: The BPR is evaluated on practical capacity, {{pct}}% of the real one: α = 0.15 and β = 4 were estimated that way (Boyles). The red dot's v/c is against real capacity.

train.freq_clip_max: ⚠ Frequency CAPPED by max frequency at {{op}} tph — demand asks for {{teo}}. Raising it does change the result; lowering the minimum does nothing. The Mohring effect is exhausted: more riders no longer bring more trains.
train.freq_clip_min: ⚠ Frequency CAPPED by min frequency at {{op}} tph — demand only asks for {{teo}}. Lowering it does change the result; raising the maximum does nothing.
train.freq_clip_libre: Frequency free at {{op}} tph: demand sets it (load / train capacity). Neither cap clips it: the minimum changes nothing until it crosses that value. The maximum also sets the platform capacity, so lowering it close to that value raises the wait before it clips.
train.anden_hint: Platform congestion (BPR): penalizes waiting once load exceeds the max-frequency capacity (v/c>1).
train.num_estaciones_hint: Sets the spacing (length ÷ this number), with a station at the CBD and at both ends when they fall exactly: 10 over 20 km gives 11 stations, every 2 km. More stations shorten the walk to the platform but lengthen the ride: the train stops at each one. There is an interior optimum.
train.costo_operacion_hint: Illustrative value, no official source yet. Enables operator cost, subsidy and self-financing in the results table.
train.factor_dia_punta_hint: Self-financing compares DAILY cost against DAILY revenue, but the model simulates only the peak hour. This factor is how much more expensive it is to run the whole day, per trip, than if the whole day had the peak's load. Off-peak service runs emptier, hence greater than 1.

equilibrium.carga_nota: Logit loading by expected flows: each group splits n·P(m) across modes, with no sampling. It is the only loading method.
equilibrium.umbrales_hint_escalones: The simplified specification (default): bike and walking penalties jump when crossing 10/20/30 and 5/15/25 min, beyond the cutoff the mode leaves the choice set, and the metro is not offered where the nearest station is the CBD one. Each rule is a step: the logsum, and with it land-use accessibility, jumps at those distances.
equilibrium.umbrales_hint_suaves: The same penalties and cutoffs, made continuous: ramps through the midpoints of the steps, the cutoff as a CMNL penalty (Martínez, Aguila and Hurtubia 2009), and the metro fading out where walking directly dominates it (Cascetta and Papola 2009). It removes the jumps in the logsum and in land use. It is another utility function: its surplus is not subtracted from the «steps» one.
equilibrium.modos_hint: Remove modes from the choice set to study stylized scenarios (e.g. Car vs Metro only).
equilibrium.modos_min: At least one mode must stay enabled.
equilibrium.verdict_ok: Converged in {{n}} of {{total}} iterations: the residual fell to {{res}}, within the {{tol}} tolerance. The results below are an equilibrium.
equilibrium.estado_pre: Not simulated yet · below, the inputs: the city and free-flow utilities
equilibrium.estado_fail: ⚠ No equilibrium · {{total}} iterations · residual {{res}} > {{tol}}: not fit for comparing scenarios
equilibrium.estado_no_tol: No convergence criterion · {{total}} fixed iterations · final residual {{res}}
equilibrium.verdict_fail: Ran out of {{total}} iterations without converging: the residual stayed at {{res}}, above the {{tol}} tolerance. Travel times are still moving, so what follows is NOT an equilibrium and cannot be used to compare scenarios. Raise the iteration cap or loosen the tolerance.
equilibrium.verdict_no_tol: No convergence criterion (tolerance 0): it ran the fixed {{total}} iterations and stopped by count, not because travel times settled. The final residual is {{res}}.
equilibrium.booting_pyodide: Initializing Pyodide in the browser (first run takes ~10–20s)…

run_status.skeleton_hint: Assigning initial demand under free flow — data will appear as soon as the first iteration completes.

presets.title: Presets
presets.diff_hint: {{n}} parameter(s) differ from the base scenario (marked ↑/↓). Grey rows are at their base value.
presets.no_diff_hint: Base scenario: no parameter differs from the default.
presets.presets_hint: Compacta, Base and Dispersa share the same population (36,000 households) and compare urban form; Metrópolis changes size, with supply at its scale.

sandbox.flow_replay_corto: The flow at each point adds up the trips originating upstream, on their way to the CBD.
sandbox.flow_replay_porque: That is why it grows toward the centre and can exceed capacity even when no single cell comes close to it.
sandbox.mode_share_by_location_stratum: Modal split by location and stratum
sandbox.city_figure_desc: Linear city of {{length}} km with {{cells}} cells. CBD at center. Bar height and color scale with travel time on {{mode}}.
sandbox.utility_caveat_corto: Compare utilities across modes within a stratum, not across strata.
sandbox.utility_caveat_porque: Each stratum has its own ASC and β, so their utilities are in different units.
sandbox.city_view_caption_corto: Above, who lives in each cell (land use); below, what was built on it (supply). These are the two inputs to the equilibrium.
sandbox.city_view_caption_porque: They share the position axis, so the same cell falls in the same column in both figures.
sandbox.mas_resultados_meta: times, tables, convergence, CO₂, share by location
sandbox.land_use_city_desc: Household distribution by stratum along the {{length}} km linear city ({{cells}} cells), as defined by the Land Use module. CBD at center.
sandbox.land_use_city_caption_post: Equilibrium composition from the Land Use module (S·Q). This is the city that feeds the transport simulation.
sandbox.land_use_city_caption_pre: Initial composition (uniform π_h mix over the city shape). Run Land Use to see the equilibrium composition.
sandbox.land_use_city_caption_none: Define the population in the Land Use module to see the distribution by stratum.

metrics_table.vc_metro_sub: max load / (max freq. × train cap.): operated over maximum frequency
metrics_table.network_load_corto: Peak corridor flow over capacity: above 1 the mode runs over capacity. For the metro, capacity is that of the maximum frequency: above 1, not even every train is enough.
metrics_table.network_load_porque: Metro adapts frequency to demand (f_op = load/K), so against its own frequency the ratio would always be 1. That is why it is measured against the maximum frequency (frec_max·K): the figure is operated over maximum frequency, and a low value is not an «empty metro» but spare trains. Above 1 is not crowding (the model has no in-vehicle crowding penalty). All three respond to population, prices and capacity, NOT to city length: in a monocentric city the section next to the CBD carries about half the trips regardless of extent.

hero.title: The linear city
hero.subtitle: Mode share by location · 0 km = west edge · center = CBD

hints.demand_corto: Each cell has three strata. Those who do not telework choose among feasible modes with a logit over times and costs.
hints.demand_porque: Feasible: walking ≤ 30 min, cycling ≤ 45 min, car only with ownership. Telework is decided beforehand and does not travel. Under deterministic assignment the whole group goes to the highest-utility mode.
hints.supply_corto: Car and bike congest with load (BPR); the metro adapts its frequency to demand on the critical link.
hints.supply_porque: Car: capacity from Greenshields (lane width reduces it) and BPR delay accumulated toward the CBD. Bike: same volume/capacity form, corrected for slope and floored at walking time. Metro: frequency capped by frec_min/frec_max, half-headway wait amplified by platform saturation, and intermediate stops inside the in-vehicle time — more stations shorten access but lengthen the ride.
hints.equilibrium_corto: MSA alternates demand and network until the times used to compute demand match those the network returns.
hints.equilibrium_porque: It averages FLOWS: the step starts at 1 and is halved every time the gap fails to fall by at least 10% (halving). The residual is the undamped gap: the largest difference, in any mode and cell, between the time the network returns when loaded with the iteration's demand and the time that demand was computed from. It converges when that stays below tolerance for 2 consecutive iterations (with tolerance 0 it runs to the iteration cap).

calibration.title: Model calibration
calibration.not_a_policy_corto: Not a policy: these are the estimated logit coefficients. Moving them changes the behavioural model, not the city or the supply.
calibration.not_a_policy_porque: A scenario where car use fell because its constant was edited says nothing about transport policy.
calibration.ratio_corto: Value of time = β time ÷ β cost. The ratios: how much more onerous a minute of waiting or access is than one on board.
calibration.ratio_porque: Chile's 2026 social prices (SNI) assign weight 2 to waiting and access; below 1 the model claims waiting bothers people less than travelling.
calibration.b_costo_warn: β cost must be negative: at 0 or positive, the value of time and the surplus are undefined.
calibration.g_asc_hint: They capture what the model does not measure (comfort, habit, status). Only differences matter: adding the same to all four changes nothing.
calibration.g_tiempo_corto: In utils per minute and per peso; all negative. A single cost β covers fuel, fare and parking.
calibration.g_tiempo_porque: Metro access and the walking mode use SEPARATE coefficients: the walk to a station is not the same as walking the whole trip.
calibration.g_penal_corto: Additive and cumulative, by minute thresholds: with «steps», a 25-min bike trip adds both the 10-min and the 20-min penalty; with «smooth», each enters as a ramp through the midpoints (Transport › Equilibrium).
calibration.g_penal_porque: With «steps», infeasibility is not a penalty: it is set by the time cutoffs, at the end of the panel.
calibration.prob_teletrabajo_hint: Share of workdays without commuting. Default 0 (no sourced figure). The policy is the multiplier, under “Economy”.
calibration.cortes_corto: With «steps», above this time the alternative leaves the choice set: it is not penalised, it stops existing. With «smooth» it stays in the set, penalised by a CMNL cutoff. They are global, not per stratum.
calibration.cortes_porque: It is a behavioural assumption, not a transport policy. Moving a cutoff changes how many alternatives there are, so it also moves the gap between logsum and max-utility surplus.

calibration_page.het_corto: How many times each stratum's time is worth relative to the low one. The middle stays fixed: changing a multiple moves the low and the high.
calibration_page.het_porque: A stratum's value of time is β time / β cost, and β time is common to all three: the multiples write the β cost of the low and the high, which also set their λ in the land bid. «Equal» leaves all three at the middle's value. The factory ones are 2 and 4, with the traveller-weighted mean anchored to the social value of time. It is a teaching tool, not a calibration.
calibration_page.title: Calibration
calibration_page.subtitle: The household's behavioral model, shared by both modules
calibration_page.intro_corto: These logit coefficients set at once the modal split, the accessibility T of the land bid and its λₕ = |β cost|.
calibration_page.intro_porque: Before simulating a city you have to decide how its residents behave. They do not belong to Transport alone: a household has a single utility function, and the one choosing a mode is the one bidding for a plot. They are not policies: moving them changes the model, not the city.
calibration_page.table_title: What the calibration implies, by stratum

row_hint.vot: β time ÷ β cost, in $/h. The same in Transport and in the land bid (1/λ).
row_hint.lambda: = |β cost|: turns transport utils into pesos when bidding.
row_hint.ruido: Scale of the bid shock, in $/month. Lower λ ⇒ wider noise in pesos.
row_hint.auto: Enters the mode-choice logit and, through the logsum, the accessibility T.

knob_effect.b_costo: Transport: value of time and sensitivity to fares and parking. Land: λₕ, which sorts the strata (Alonso gradient), and the accessibility T.
knob_effect.b_tiempo: Transport: the value of time and the split between fast and slow modes. Land: the accessibility T, since it changes each cell's logsum.
knob_effect.asc: Transport: the modal split. Land: the accessibility T, through the same logsum.
knob_effect.prob_auto: Transport: who can choose the car. Land: each stratum's accessibility T; with equal λ, it leaves the high stratum somewhat farther from the center.

calibration_page.stale_note: Any change here makes the Transport, Land use and City in equilibrium results stale: each page flags it and offers to rerun.
calibration_page.summary: The logit coefficients are edited on the Calibration page: they also set land use's accessibility and λ.
calibration_page.mu_corto: Precision of the home-choice noise (Martínez, eq. 4.2), common to all strata: the bid noise is 1/(μ·λ_h). It is set on the Land use page.
calibration_page.mu_porque: There is no transferable μ: it is estimated from observed location by stratum (bid-auction logit, Martínez 2018 §9.3) and, if rents are observed, the rent equation identifies the scale (Lerman and Kern 1983). Here it is a scenario value; higher μ ⇒ a more segregated city. Only μ·α and μ·ρ are identified: with α fixed at 1, moving μ scales the sensitivity to accessibility and to density at once. Until Oct-2026 it was 1/√44, by an analogy with 44 independent trip shocks that does not hold: those shocks are already integrated in the logsum.

demand_inspector.title: Utility inspector — multinomial logit
demand_inspector.interpretation: V = the mode's systematic utility, the observed part of U = V + ε. It is in utils: only differences across modes matter — ~1 util of advantage ≈ 2.7× more likely. P = choice probability of THIS agent (not the system's mode share).
demand_inspector.interpretation_corto: V is the observed utility, in utils: only differences across modes matter. P is this agent's probability, not the system's mode share.
demand_inspector.interpretation_porque: U = V + ε. ~1 util of advantage ≈ 2.7× more likely.

utility_breakdown.v_title: V — the mode's systematic utility, in utils
utility_breakdown.p_title: P — choice probability of this agent

stratum_distribution.aria: Spatial distribution of households by stratum

land_use.title: Land use
land_use.poblacion_total_corto: Total population ≈ {{total}} = length × mean density ({{dens}} pop/km): it sets how many households there are.
land_use.poblacion_total_porque: Per-cell density is a consequence of supply (S/Δx), not an imposed gradient.
land_use.bidrent_corto: The bid's accessibility is the mode-choice logsum, monthly and with weight 1; λ_h = |b_cost_h| turns it into pesos.
land_use.bidrent_porque: The logsum is that household's expected trip utility; it is made monthly with the stratum's expected trips (44 × the share that does not telework: teleworkers do not value being close to the CBD). With λ_h the value of time is the same as in Transport: one household, one utility function.
land_use.subtitle: Alonso-Muth-Mills model
land_use.info_standalone: Solves the Alonso equilibrium with Transport's accessibility: the mode-choice logsum at free flow, per stratum, monthly. No congestion.
land_use.info_coupled: Iterates land use ↔ transport until T stabilizes.
land_use.outer_iter_hint: Each iteration runs the full transport MSA. Keep small in class.
land_use.run_placeholder: Run the solver to see the spatial assignment.
land_use.heading_distribution: Spatial distribution of households by stratum
land_use.trajectory_residual_desc: max |T_new − T|/λₕ: map gap in $/household-month; converges below 100
land_use.densidad_hint: Each cell's density is set by the housing supply, S/Δx: equilibrium decides who lives in each cell, not how many.
land_use.oferta_sigma_hint: Shape of housing supply: low = compact city (near CBD), high = sprawling.
land_use.forma_hint_normal: Bell centered on the CBD: compact monocentric.
land_use.forma_hint_uniforme: Flat density along the whole corridor (homogeneous suburb).
land_use.forma_hint_exponencial: Density ∝ e^(−d/σ): decays from the CBD (von Thünen).
land_use.forma_hint_bimodal: Two peaks: polycentric city with subcenters.
land_use.forma_hint_meseta: Flat-density core with a sharp edge: compact city with a boundary.
land_use.shape_preview_caption: Housing supply profile S(d) for the current parameters. Run the equilibrium to see how the strata sort over this city.
land_use.initial_pop_caption_corto: Initial state: every cell has the same strata mix (the global proportions), over the supply profile S(d).
land_use.initial_pop_caption_porque: When the equilibrium runs, bid-rent sorts this mix in space: the strata that value the center most win the parcels near the CBD.
land_use.metrics_caption: Mean distance to the CBD by stratum (the highest-valuation stratum wins the center) · Theil (0 = mixed, 1 = fully segregated)
land_use.forma_hint_valle: Little space at the center, lots at the periphery: density grows with distance (inverted triangle).
land_use.oferta_sigma_na: Not applicable to the uniform shape (flat density).
land_use.y_na_corto: Income is not here: it does not change where any stratum lives.
land_use.y_na_link: It is edited in Calibration, which explains why.
land_use.intro: Bid-rent: households that value accessibility to the center most outbid the rest for parcels near the CBD and push the others to the periphery.
land_use.relation: This module solves land use ONLY, with transport fixed at free flow. For the full land ↔ transport loop, see “City at equilibrium”.
land_use.placeholder_title: Land use · the auction for space
land_use.placeholder_desc_corto: Each stratum bids according to its valuation of accessibility and its disutility of density; the one with the highest value of time wins the center.
land_use.placeholder_desc_porque: In pesos, accessibility weighs T/λ and density ρ·d/λ, with d the density relative to the mean. The other strata sort toward the periphery.
land_use.lambda_values_corto: λ = {{l1}} · {{l2}} · {{l3}} utils/$: each stratum's |b_cost|. It moves from the Calibration page.
land_use.lambda_values_porque: Changing b_cost changes both λ (the value of time used to bid) and the accessibility T. A common scale of all three does not move the allocation, only the rent unit.
land_use.rho_corto: Disutility of the cell's relative density; it enters in pesos as ρ/λ_h. 0 by default (pure Alonso); near 28 the allocation inverts.
land_use.rho_porque: No source in the original model. Density is relative (the cell's over the city mean), so its effect does not change with population. Since it is divided by λ_h, the high stratum pays more for low density. Raising it mixes the city and flattens rents; the ≈28 threshold holds for the default supply, and above it the rich end up in the periphery.
land_use.param_mu: μ · precision of the location noise
land_use.mu_corto: Higher μ ⇒ less noise in choosing a home: each stratum keeps its band and the city segregates.
land_use.mu_porque: The bid noise is 1/(μ·λ_h) $/month. With low μ idiosyncratic taste dominates and strata mix; with high μ accessibility dominates and the stratum that values time most wins the center. There is no transferable μ: it is calibrated against observed location by stratum (bid-auction logit, Martínez 2018 §9.3); in Santiago, against distance to the employment center by income, because segregation there is sectoral. Only μ·ρ is identified: moving μ also scales the density penalty.

bid_price.footer: Relative · 0 = minimum · Δ {{delta}} (price up to a constant)
bid_price.units_logit: Pesos per month: the expected maximum of the bids y + f/λ (Martínez, eq. 4.27).

compare.subtitle: Up to 4 configurations side by side · pick the baseline with ○ on each card

compare.flow_no_profile: Mode «{{mode}}» has no per-cell demand profile.

compare.transport_hint_porque: No relocation: relocation is the «City at equilibrium» lens.
compare.base_sin_resultado: The base has no transport result: run it first.

cp.bienestar: Δ Surplus vs its own empty network ($/month)
cp.caption: Final-equilibrium metrics for each scenario (last outer iteration). Green/red = better/worse than the baseline per metric direction. «Δ Surplus vs baseline» is the transport welfare change between scenarios: each one's level minus the baseline's, only if they share modes, β, teleworking and population. «vs its own empty network» compares each scenario with itself (congestion against the Mohring effect) and is not subtracted across scenarios: prices almost cancel out in it.

bien.title: Welfare · Δ vs baseline
bien.caption: Peak hour, whole city. Only the Δ against the baseline: the level has an arbitrary zero, set by the ASCs. Surplus uses the measure of the assignment method (logsum or maximum utility), and social welfare adds revenue and subtracts operating cost (Welfare chapter of the tutorial).
bien.incomparable: ⚠ {{nombre}}: its surplus cannot be subtracted from the baseline's because {{razon}}.

diff.title: What differs between scenarios
diff.need_two: Configure at least two scenarios to see the differences.
diff.identical: The configured scenarios are identical: there is no input difference to explain.
diff.calibracion: Stratum calibration (β, ASC, penalties, car ownership, telework)

coupled.title: City at equilibrium
coupled.lede_corto: Congestion reshuffles households and the new locations change demand. This page compares the equilibrium without feedback with the coupled one.
coupled.lede_porque: Transport and land use are not independent systems: demand, in turn, reshapes the network.
coupled.placeholder: Select a scenario and press «Run scenario».
coupled.without_feedback_hint: First pass of the coupled loop: land use is solved with travel times equal to distance, unaware of congestion.
coupled.with_feedback_hint: Reconciled equilibrium: land and transport iterate mutually until stable. Differences reveal the feedback effect.
coupled.diff_hint: Households of each stratum in the final equilibrium minus the first round. Each cell's supply does not change, so in every cell the three curves add up to zero: what one stratum gains another loses.
coupled.source_preset_label: Or try a predefined scenario (quick test)
coupled.custom_desc: Run the loop with the city you set up in the Transport and Land Use modules.
coupled.preset_detail_hint: The parameters the preset moves: whether the city is compact or sprawling, and whether the policy favors cars, bikes or the metro.
coupled.preset_detail_hint_custom: These parameters come from your Transport (Sandbox) and Land Use modules. To change them, adjust them in those modules and come back here.
coupled.convergence_corto: The residual measures how much accessibility T changes between rounds, in $/household-month; near 0, land and transport are in mutual equilibrium.
coupled.convergence_porque: T is the logsum accessibility of each stratum and cell. The gap is divided by λ_h to express it in pesos, so the tolerance means the same for all three strata.

compact_toll.title: Compact + Road Pricing
compact_toll.desc: Dense city with congestion pricing. Classic European scenario.

sparse_proauto.title: Sparse + Pro-Auto
sparse_proauto.desc: Sprawled city with abundant road infra. US scenario.

base_probici.title: Base + Pro-Bike
base_probici.desc: Medium city with wide bike lanes and disincentivized parking.

compact_metro.title: Compact + Max Metro
compact_metro.desc: Dense city with maximum metro frequency and many stations.

interp.segregation_up_porque: Congestion pushes high-time-value strata to the center; low-value ones migrate to the periphery.
interp.segregation_down: Feedback reduced segregation by Δ={{delta}}. Spatial reshuffle diluted the initial stratum concentration.
interp.welfare_regressive: Regressive: the low stratum's monthly burden changed {{bajo}} pp (now {{cargaBajo}}% of its income); the high stratum's, {{alto}} pp.
interp.welfare_progressive: Progressive: the low stratum's monthly burden changed {{bajo}} pp (now {{cargaBajo}}% of its income); the high stratum's, {{alto}} pp.
interp.accessibility_body: Mean time vs. no feedback: high {{alto}} min, low {{bajo}} min. The low stratum ends at {{tBajo}} min.
interp.stable_body: Outer iterations did not meaningfully shift aggregate metrics. Feedback was weak in this scenario — try a more aggressive policy.

coupled.placeholder_desc_corto: The outer loop alternates land (bid-rent over accessibility T) and transport (MSA) until T stabilizes.
coupled.placeholder_desc_porque: Each round: (1) bid-rent allocates households given accessibility T(i); (2) that population runs the transport equilibrium (MSA); (3) T is recomputed on the loaded network.

coupled_metrics.segregation_hint: Theil index. 0 = integrated city, 1 = perfect segregation. Drops when policy brings strata together; rises if the market pulls them apart.
coupled_metrics.welfare_hint: Average chosen-mode utility per stratum. Rises under policies that reduce time or cost for the average agent.
coupled_metrics.accessibility_hint: Hansen index per stratum: Σ exp(−α·T). Larger = destinations closer in generalized cost. Compare deltas, not absolute values.

eqt.title: Equilibrium metrics
eqt.input_note: Metrics tagged «input» are scenario data and do not change with feedback.
eqt.welfare_total_sub: Σ households · ΔCS vs empty network ($/month) · transport only
eqt.caveat_corto: The surplus Δ measures efficiency (willingness to pay) vs. the empty network, not interpersonal welfare. For the distributional reading, look at burden and time.
eqt.caveat_porque: It compares the observed logsum against the same network with zero demand (BPR at 0, train at minimum frequency): Δ<0 ⇒ congestion dominates; Δ>0 ⇒ the Mohring effect dominates (more demand ⇒ higher frequency ⇒ less waiting). It is in $/household-month (44 trips; teleworkers count as 0), and $1 is worth differently to each stratum (b_costo varies ~3.9×). It counts transport only, without land rents: it is a lower bound of the benefit (Martínez 2018, §10.10).

convergence.sub_relativa: average excess cost / mean travel time · % · should tend to 0
convergence.modal_split_sub: Evolution of modal split while MSA smooths (cumulative trips per mode)

network.title: Road network · saturation by segment
network.aria: Linear city road network with auto, metro and bike

msa.aria: Interactive diagram of the MSA algorithm
msa.initial_desc: First iteration: agents assume no congestion. Times = distance / free-flow speed.
msa.logit_desc: Each agent evaluates utility per mode and chooses with probability proportional to exp(V_m).
msa.congestion_desc: Given assigned demand, times are recomputed with BPR (auto, bike) or platform saturation (metro).
msa.smooth_desc: To avoid oscillation, the new flow x* is mixed with the current one with a step α that starts at 1 and halves every time the gap fails to fall by at least 10% (Boyles §8.3.5). With «Logit — sampling» the times are averaged with weight 1/(n+1).
msa.check_desc: If the gap — what the loaded network returns against the times the demand was computed with — stays below the tolerance for two iterations in a row, equilibrium is reached.
msa.done_desc: Travel times are consistent with the modal assignment they induce.

coupled.aria: Interactive diagram of the land-use↔transport coupled loop
coupled.config_desc: City, strata, infrastructure and land-use parameters. Initial T = the empty network's accessibility (−44 · logsum at free flow).
coupled.landuse_desc: Solves the Alonso equilibrium: each stratum gets a distribution Q over parcels balancing price, accessibility and density.
coupled.assign_desc: From Q the population is built deterministically: each stratum's households in each parcel, respecting the supply S_i.
coupled.transport_desc: With the new population, a full transport equilibrium runs; its output is a new T[h, i] matrix.
coupled.check_desc: The new T is compared with the current one, in pesos (÷λ_h). Tolerance of 100 $/household-month; it converges only if the MSA and the auction converged too.
coupled.done_desc: Land use and transport are consistent: neither changes when the other is updated.

agg.ocupacion_metro_nota: (passenger-km over those offered; the service runs both ways and everyone heads to the centre, so 50% is full in the loaded direction)
agg.peaje_pigou_nota: (maximum {{max}}/km next to the centre · currently charged {{actual}}/km)
agg.peaje_pigou_porque: It is the marginal external cost of congestion: the delay one more car imposes on everyone already on the link, which the driver does not pay. Charging it makes each driver decide with the cost caused to the city, not only their own. It is an indicator on this run's demand: if it were charged, some cars would leave the corridor and the toll would fall; the optimum is where that adjustment stops. It only counts delay: the extra fuel congestion makes others burn is left out.
agg.frecuencia_mohring_porque: The model runs the metro at just the frequency needed to fit the load of the critical section. Mohring's answers another question: the one that minimises what users spend waiting plus what operating costs. It grows with the square root of demand, not in proportion. If it is higher than the operated one, adding trains saves more waiting than it costs. It depends on the cost per train-km, which is an illustrative value, and ignores the capacity cap and platform congestion. It is an indicator on this run's demand, not another equilibrium.

grupo.transferencias_glosa: they change pockets: not resources consumed
grupo.beneficio_glosa: resource savings and consumer surplus are alternatives, not addends

agg.costo_recursos_nota: (time at the social VoT + car and metro operation + CO₂ + investment)
agg.costo_recursos_porque: This is the other route to measuring the benefit, and the one MESPIVU uses: the saving in total resource consumption between the base and the project. Generalised cost and consumer surplus look at the trip from the user's side, and count what they pay even when that payment consumes nothing: the toll, parking, the fare and the fuel tax leave one pocket and enter another. Only what society actually spends goes in here, at social prices, and time goes at the social value, not each stratum's. Its Δ with the sign flipped is the resource saving. They are not an identity, and may disagree even in sign: with Tarificación Vial (200 $/km) the resource cost falls by 303 thousand —a saving— while social welfare falls by 727 thousand. The resource cost only counts time, operation and CO₂; not what is lost by those who switch to a mode they liked less, which the surplus does capture.

aprendizaje.title: Day-to-day learning
aprendizaje.subtitle: A person who does not know travel times and learns them from experience — and only experiences the mode they chose.
aprendizaje.sin_corrida: This page uses equilibrium travel times. Run the Transport module first and come back: the experiment is then instantaneous.
aprendizaje.aviso_margen: Careful with Φ: the margin P* − ½ is {{margen}}, so it divides by almost nothing and amplifies any difference. Look at S and the inverted share too.
aprendizaje.celda_hint: Where the person lives. The CBD sits at the city centre.
aprendizaje.decaimiento_hint: 0 averages the whole history evenly; higher values look only at recent days. Guevara, Tang and Gao (2018) estimate 1.28.
aprendizaje.k_shocks_hint: The first k times they use the better mode come out worse. If they quit early they never get all of them.
aprendizaje.dias_hint: The IBL cost grows with the square of the horizon.

fig.titulo: Mean share of the better mode, day by day
fig.titulo_una: One replica: a single person's history
fig.nota: Each point is the mean across replicas of the probability of choosing the better mode that day. It comes out smooth even though no individual history is: belief only changes on days the person uses the mode, and the shock lands the first time they choose it, which is not the same day for everyone. Switch to «one replica» to see the real shape.
fig.nota_una: A single history, not averaged. The curve is a step function because belief only changes on days the person uses the mode: in between, P(t) is flat. The shock lands the first time they choose the better mode — not necessarily day 1 — and then dilutes as good experiences accumulate. It is the same simulation as the mean.

aprendizaje.dias_ciudad_hint: Deliberately short: the cost grows with the square and the network is solved every day. The published reports use 250.

ciudad.dispersion_sub: times the binomial; 1 = history made no difference
ciudad.brecha: They believe they are better off by
ciudad.abandono_sub: could use it and never did
ciudad.quien_paga_meta: by which mode is THEIR best

teoria.intro: Without knowing what each component is, a Φ of 1.01 or a Δ* of 39.8 min says nothing. These are the equations the module runs and the meaning of every variable.

percibido.texto: Instance-based learning: the time a person believes a mode takes is the weighted average of the times they actually experienced on it. Days they did not choose it do not count — that asymmetry is where everything else comes from.

sim.b: the time person n believes mode i takes when deciding on day t
sim.x: the time they actually experienced on that mode on day t′
sim.a: 1 if they chose mode i that day, 0 otherwise
sim.w: how much day t′ weighs in today's belief
sim.d: memory decay: 0 averages the whole history evenly, higher values look almost only at recent days

eleccion.texto: The simulator's utility, corrected by the gap between belief and the reference time. Everything that is not travel time — modal constants, cost, penalties — already sits inside the reference utility and is not relearned.

sim.vref: utility of mode i at the day-0 reference times
sim.beta: travel time coefficient, in utils per minute (negative)
sim.tau: reference travel time of mode i, the equilibrium one
sim.mu: the logit scale. The simulator normalises it to 1 and the β coefficients absorb it

ventaja.texto: How much the better mode beats the other, and what someone who knows the times would choose. Read in minutes the advantage does not depend on the logit scale; the probability does.

sim.dv: advantage of the better mode over the other, in utils
sim.A: the same advantage in minutes — the scale-free form
sim.pestrella: probability of choosing the better mode with perfect information: the ceiling learning is measured against

phi.texto: The central indicator. It is 1 if learning reproduced the informed choice, 0 if the person ended up flipping a coin, and negative if it inverted: on average they pick the worse mode. It can exceed 1, and that is not an error — it means they chose the good mode more often than the informed benchmark. Careful when the denominator is small: Φ then amplifies any difference.

sim.S: mean share of the mode that truly is better
sim.uniforme: the indifference point: ½ with two modes, and the uniform split across the J feasible modes when there are more
sim.phi: the fraction of the true advantage that survives learning

racha.texto: If the first times they use the better mode come out worse, how much does it take to change behaviour? The threshold is exact and does not depend on the logit scale: it follows only from the advantage in minutes and from memory. What does depend on scale is how abrupt the fall is once it is crossed.

sim.k: how many of the first uses of the better mode come out worse
sim.delta: how much worse each of those is, in minutes
sim.wk: how much the bad streak weighs against the initial belief
sim.dcritico: the shock that leaves the perceived advantage exactly at zero
sim.ppost: probability of choosing the better mode again right after the k-th hit. If it stays very low the person stops sampling it and never learns it is no longer bad

dispersion.titulo: 6. How much history separated equal people
dispersion.texto: Only meaningful for the whole city. People with the same stratum, cell and car ownership share the same equilibrium probability: if they all chose with it, the variance of their share would be the binomial. Above 1 is pure path dependence.

sim.R: ratio of observed spread to the spread chance alone would explain
sim.pbarra: mean share of the group of identical people
sim.U: the final days over which the share is measured

brecha.titulo: 7. What is believed versus what is lived
brecha.texto: The utility used to decide is not the one experienced: since only the chosen mode is observed, and what looks good is chosen, the belief ends up biased in its favour. Measured in travel minutes, it is how much better people believe they are than they actually are.

sim.B: the gap, in travel minutes per person
sim.vdec: perceived utility of the chosen mode, the one used to decide
sim.vexp: true utility of that same trip, with the real travel time

precios_sociales.corto: From the SNI annual report (MDSF). When the new report is published, update them here.
precios_sociales.porque: They only enter the appraisal —resource cost, social generalised cost and socially weighted surplus—, never mode choice: changing them does not move the equilibrium, but you must simulate again for the aggregates to pick them up. They travel with the exported scenario, so an old run can be reproduced with the prices of its year. Roughness (IRI) is not a price and is not in the report: it is the assumption MESPIVU uses for lubricants, tyres, parts and maintenance; at 0 it gives a floor.

ingreso.pregunta: Why does income not change where each stratum lives?
ingreso.respuesta: Because in the land auction income is a constant of the stratum, and what decides who wins each parcel is the DIFFERENCE in bids between parcels. Stratum h's willingness to pay for parcel i is:
ingreso.paso_constante: y_h is the same on every parcel: raising it raises the stratum's bid across the whole city equally, favouring no parcel.
ingreso.paso_reserva: u_h, the reservation utility, adjusts in equilibrium until the stratum places exactly all its households. If y_h rises by Δ, u_h rises by λ_h·Δ and the bid is identical: neither location nor rents change.
ingreso.paso_orden: What orders the city is what DOES vary between parcels: accessibility in money, T/λ_h, and density, ρ/λ_h. That is why each stratum's value of time rules, not its income.
ingreso.pasos_titulo: Step by step: where income cancels out
ingreso.paso1: The bid. It is the willingness to pay above: income enters additively, the same on every parcel.
ingreso.paso2: The auction. Each parcel goes to the highest bidder; with Gumbel noise, the probability that stratum h wins is a logit ACROSS STRATA. Here income does enter and does not cancel: with u_h given, a richer stratum would win more parcels across the whole city.
ingreso.paso3: The equilibrium. But u_h is not given: the city is closed, each stratum has H_h households and all must be located. That condition is what determines u_h.
ingreso.paso4: The income change. Raise each stratum's income by any amount Δ_h (different per stratum) and try the reservation utility shifted by λ_h·Δ_h. The bid is identical:
ingreso.paso5: The conclusion. With the same bids the auction allocates the same: Q does not change, the condition of step 3 still holds and the shifted utility is the new equilibrium. Rents do not change either, since they are the expected maximum of those same bids. The extra income shows up entirely in u_h: more welfare, same location.
ingreso.ejemplo: Example: with the low stratum at $1M, the high stratum earning $3M or $10M gives the same city. The $7M difference raises its reservation utility by λ_high·$7M and nothing else. To represent a «richer» high stratum in location, move what income does to its preferences: the value of time (the multiples above), which is what steepens its bid towards the centre.
ingreso.supuesto: The result rests on two model assumptions: the bid is linear in income (quasi-linear utility, no income effect) and each stratum's population is fixed. In an open city, with u_h given, income would move location. The core checks it in a test: changing incomes does not move the allocation.
ingreso.donde_importa: Where it does matter: the monthly transport burden (cost / income) in «City in equilibrium» divides by these values. And each stratum's reservation utility rises with its income: those who earn more live better, but in the same place.

escenario.desde_base: Each preset builds the scenario from the base: it discards manual adjustments and keeps only the calibration.
escenario.ajustes: ⚠ This scenario has manual adjustments: it is not the preset as is. Choosing a preset discards them.

inversion.corto: Unit costs of infrastructure, so that adding supply is not free.
inversion.aviso_cero: ⚠ All costs are zero: a lane, a station or more cycleway cost nothing, and policies that add capacity are favoured.
inversion.porque: The scenario's whole stock is valued: lanes × city length, stations, cycleway capacity × length, and the premium of a cleaner fleet in proportion to how much its emission factor falls. That capital is annualised with the social discount rate (under Social prices) and the service life, and divided by the equivalent peak hours of the year to be on the same basis as the rest of the table. It enters the resource cost and is subtracted from social welfare; it does not change mode choice. Costs start at zero because there is no source for them: the 20 years are the horizon MESPIVU recommends for infrastructure, and the 500 peak hours a year (250 days times 2) are an assumption.
